name: MarkWest Arkoma Connector Pipeline
researcher_notes: The line is already built, so this is a gap in the tracker, not a new project. The Energy Information Administration pipeline projects table for August 2026 (sheet Historical Projects (1996-2024), Excel row 606, project name MarkWest Arkoma Connector Pipeline Project, operator MarkWest Pioneer LLC) lists it as completed July 14, 2009, with 50 miles, 24 inch diameter, 638 million cubic feet per day of added capacity, a cost of 75 million dollars, and Federal Energy Regulatory Commission docket CP08-404. A Natural Gas Intelligence article from 2008 independently describes about 50 miles from the Woodford Shale area in southeastern Oklahoma to the proposed Midcontinent Express Pipeline interconnect at Bennington. The same article is said in the candidate note to give up to 625,000 Dth per day; I did not find that figure in the text I could read, so capacity uses the EIA figure. Not a match to P0318 (Arkoma Residue Capacity, a cancelled Tall Oak project) or P0213 and P0284, which only share Bennington as an endpoint. Start point is described as near Coalgate per the candidate note; the sources I read say only the Woodford Shale area. The EIA row and the Natural Gas Intelligence article may share one origin in the FERC filing, so independence is moderate. Owner MarkWest Pioneer LLC has no existing entity in the tracker; no parent confirmed. No route found; no official GIS checked. Length is over the 25 km add threshold.
